item.title: It is 2026. Why are your object mappings still strings?
item.description:
The setup

Mapping one Java object to another is routine work in most apps, and MapStruct, the standard tool for it, still has you name each field with a string: @Mapping(source = "customerName", target = "fullName"). Those two names are what the whole mapping turns on, and the compiler never reads them.

MapStruct earned its place. Ten years, a huge adopter base, a bug list that converged long ago, and it generates genuinely fast code; I reach for it too. Those strings are just the one piece of its 2014 design that aged badly.

item.title: From a Monocle port to one fluent type: how Telescope happened
item.description: Telescope is a Java deep-copy DSL for records and POJOs. You build a path through an immutable graph, then read it, write it, update it, traverse it, convert it, or thread an effect through it. No hand-written copy constructors. No mention of Iso, Lens, Prism, Affine, or Traversal anywhere in your code. The end-state is one method-ref chain on the runtime DSL, or one fluent chain on the generated navigator.
